name: Congenital Herpes Simplex Virus Infection

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Neonatal Herpes Simplex Virus Infection Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of vesicular skin lesions or mucocutaneous ulcerations in neonate
Isolation of herpes simplex virus by PCR or culture from skin, mucous membranes, cerebrospinal fluid, or blood
Signs of central nervous system involvement such as seizures or encephalitis
Maternal history of genital herpes or primary HSV infection during pregnancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus virological confirmation of HSV infection
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical to initiate antiviral therapy and reduce morbidity and mortality.

laboratory: Positive HSV PCR from skin lesions, CSF, blood or mucous membranes
CSF pleocytosis with elevated protein in CNS involvement
Thrombocytopenia and elevated liver enzymes in disseminated disease
imaging: MRI brain showing temporal lobe hyperintensities consistent with herpes encephalitis
Chest X-ray showing pneumonitis in respiratory involvement
other: Maternal serology may show recent HSV infection
Histopathology of skin lesions showing multinucleated giant cells

distinguishingFeatures: Vesicular lesions in different stages of healing
PCR positive for VZV, negative for HSV
Petechiae and hepatosplenomegaly without vesicular lesions

redFlags: Rapid progression to encephalitis with seizures
Failure to respond to antiviral therapy within 48-72 hours
references: Kimberlin DW. Neonatal herpes simplex infection. Clin Microbiol Rev. 2004 Oct;17(4):1-13.
Whitley RJ. Herpes simplex virus infections of the newborn. Semin Perinatol. 1990 Apr;14(2):90-100.
American Academy of Pediatrics. Red Book: 2021 Report of the Committee on Infectious Diseases.
